title: 0652-inferring-team-strengths-discrete-markov-random-field
universal_lens: The discrete Markov Random Field unifies latent state transitions and emission probabilities into a single non-convex energy landscape. By modeling offensive/defensive strengths as discrete states, the system maps combinatorial scoreline generation to a probabilistic graphical model, exposing fundamental limitations in low-dimensional discrete approximations of continuous athletic dynamics.
gsi_mapping: GSI maps the EM objective function to a Bayesian posterior over team latent variables. Loopy belief propagation serves as an approximate conformal inference engine, yielding posterior predictive distributions for goal totals. The discrete conditional emission matrices act as non-parametric likelihood kernels bypassing strict Poisson assumptions.
gse_mapping: GSE utilizes the Markov transition matrices (Ω, Δ) to model week-to-week situational persistence. The inferred discrete offensive/defensive states represent compact tactical regimes. The failure of this discrete topology to beat Elo highlights the necessity for continuous-state dynamical systems in capturing real-time athletic momentum.

primitives.name: Discrete Latent Strength MRF
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model - Latent variables: per team t, per date d: offensive strength O_{t,d} ∈ S and defensive strength D_{t,d} ∈ S (discrete states, 4 used for plotting).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: O_{t,d}, D_{t,d}: dimensionless discrete latent state indices; S: finite state space cardinality; t: team identifier; d: temporal index (week)
primitives.assumptions: Team strengths are piecewise constant within discrete states and evolve according to first-order Markovian dynamics.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when true athletic performance evolves continuously, causing quantization errors that degrade predictive power against simpler continuous baselines like Elo.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE's regime-switching models, mapping discrete states to tactical formations or roster configurations.
layer2.telemetry: Joint log-likelihood convergence paths across multiple random restarts.

primitives.name: Freely Parameterized Emission Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Emission: home goals ~ Ψ(offense_home, defense_away); away goals ~ Γ(offense_away, defense_home) — freely parameterized discrete conditional distributions (NOT assumed Poisson).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Ψ, Γ: conditional probability mass functions over integer goal counts; dimensionless probabilities summing to 1.
primitives.assumptions: Goal generation is conditionally independent given the latent offensive and defensive states of the participating teams.
primitives.breakdown_regime: High-variance overfitting occurs due to sparse data in the joint state space, leading to degenerate emission matrices without heavy regularization.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's non-parametric scoring kernels, allowing empirical deviation from standard Poisson shot-conversion models.
layer2.telemetry: Deviation metrics between learned Ψ_{1,2,g} and matched theoretical Poisson distributions.

primitives.name: Non-Convex EM with Loopy BP
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Inference: EM with loopy belief propagation in the E-step; non-convex — 8 random restarts give different joint log-likelihood paths (Figure 7); regularization needed.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Q: expected complete-data log-likelihood (nats); θ: model parameters (transition/emission matrices); Z: latent state assignments; X: observed scorelines.
primitives.assumptions: The graphical model contains loops requiring approximate inference via message passing, and the Q-function provides a valid lower bound surrogate.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Training becomes fragile and highly dependent on initialization; distinct local optima prevent reliable recovery of true underlying team strengths.

layer2.mapping: Directly maps to GSE's variational inference pipelines, highlighting the computational cost of exact marginalization in dense sports graphs.
layer2.telemetry: Variance of final log-likelihood across 8 independent coordinate-ascent initializations.

The foundational operator here is the Discrete Markov Random Field, which attempts to compress continuous athletic evolution into a finite set of latent offensive and defensive states. Mathematically, this constructs a high-dimensional energy landscape where the Expectation-Maximization algorithm seeks global maxima. However, the introduction of loopy belief propagation introduces approximation errors inherent to cyclic graphical dependencies. The dualities emerge between the expressive power of freely parameterized emission kernels—which successfully capture non-Poissonian goal distributions—and the severe fragility of the optimization routine. The failure mode is elegantly exposed by the non-convexity: eight identical training runs yield divergent joint log-likelihood paths, proving the landscape is riddled with local optima. Consequently, the discrete restriction acts as a binding constraint, creating a quantization bias that systematically underperforms the smooth, continuous updates of the Elo rating system. This demonstrates that while the structural unification of time-varying strengths and scoreline emissions is mathematically sound, the discrete topological choice fundamentally limits its epistemic utility in low-scoring sports environments.
